title: Polynomial-Time Computability of Stored Visits
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine, let $	au$ be one of its work tapes, and let $t$ assign a natural number to each bit string. If the function that maps $z$ to the unary bit string of length $t(z)$ is polynomial-time computable, then the function that maps $z$ to the stored visit code for tape $	au$ at time $t(z)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state binary Turing machine
$	au$ is a work tape of $M$
$t$ is a function from bit strings to natural numbers
The unary string of length $t(z)$ is polynomial-time computable as a function of $z$
replaced: For every work tape and polynomial-time unary time producer, the stored visit code at the produced time is polynomial-time computable, read by the charged sequential field reader.
